questions.text:
Gunsutron (chromosomes) ke sandarbh mein sahi kathan ka chayan kijiye:
(i) Janakon se aanuvanshik soochana ko agli peedhi tak pahunchate hain.
(ii) Dhaage ki tarah ki sanrachnaen jo jantu koshika ke kendrak ke andar sthit hote hain.
(iii) Manav yugmakon mein sada yugm (jore) ke roop mein paaye jaate hain.
(iv) Koshika vibhajan prakram mein aaveshthit (shamil) rahte hain.
questions.text_english:
Select the correct statement(s) regarding chromosomes:
(i) They carry genetic information from parents to the next generation.
(ii) They are thread-like structures found inside the nucleus of animal cells.
(iii) In human gametes, they are always found in pairs.
(iv) They are involved in the process of cell division.
questions.solution: Option D is correct because statements (i), (ii), and (iv) are true about chromosomes. Statement (iii) is incorrect because in human gametes (sperm and egg), chromosomes are haploid (23 single chromosomes), not in pairs. Pairs (diploid) are found in somatic cells.
questions.solution_hindi: Vikalp D sahi hai. Kathan (i), (ii) aur (iv) gunsutron ke baare mein satya hain. Kathan (iii) galat hai kyonki manav yugmakon (shukranu aur and) mein gunsutra agunit (23 ekal) hote hain, jodon mein nahin.

questions.text: Patti ki kaun-si sanrachna mukhya roop se gaso ke vinimay hetu uttardayi hai?
questions.text_english: Which structure of the leaf is primarily responsible for gaseous exchange?
questions.solution: Option B (Stomata) is correct. Stomata are tiny pores on leaf surfaces that allow exchange of gases (oxygen and carbon dioxide) and water vapor between the plant and the atmosphere.
questions.solution_hindi: Vikalp B (Randhra/Stomata) sahi hai. Randhra patti ki satth par sthit sukshma chhidra hote hain jo gaso ke aadan-pradan mein sahayak hote hain.

questions.text: Ek kisan apne khet mein pahle se ug rahe kele ke paudhon ke saman aanuvanshikata vale paudhon ko ugana chahta hai. Is uddeshya ki prapti ke liye aap kaun-si vidhi ka sujhav denge?
questions.text_english: A farmer wants to grow plants with the same genetic makeup as existing banana plants in his field. Which method would you suggest for this purpose?
questions.solution: Option C (Vegetative propagation) is correct. This method produces offspring genetically identical to the parent (clones). Banana plants are commonly propagated through vegetative methods like suckers or tissue culture to maintain desired traits.
questions.solution_hindi: Vikalp C (Kayik Pravardhan) sahi hai. Is vidhi dwara utpann santati janak paudhe ki aanuvaanshik roop se samroop (clone) hoti hai. Kele ke paudhe kayik pravrdhan dwara ugaye jaate hain.

questions.text_english: Which of the following sets is NOT biodegradable?

options.A: Sabjiyon ke chilke, mrit pattiyaan, kagaj

questions.text_english: The human brain has many parts that help in various functions, responses, and integration. Identify the part responsible for performing voluntary actions with precision:
questions.solution: Option B (Cerebellum) is correct. The cerebellum maintains balance, posture, and coordinates voluntary movements with precision. The cerebrum controls voluntary actions but the cerebellum ensures their precision and coordination.
questions.solution_hindi: Vikalp B (Anumastishk) sahi hai. Anumastishk santulan, mudra evam aichchhik gatividhiyon ko parishuddhata se karne ke liye uttardayi hai.

questions.text_english: Select the appropriate statement regarding Spirogyra, Euglena, and Hydra:

options.A: Sabhi mein laingik janan hota hai.

questions.text: Agnyashay dwara agnyashayik ras sravit kiya jaata hai jismein kuchh vishesh enzymes hote hain jo bhojan ke paachan mein sahayak hain. Nimnlikhit mein se sahi vikalp ka chayan kijiye:
questions.text_english: The pancreas secretes pancreatic juice containing specific enzymes that aid digestion. Select the correct option:

options.A: Trypsin emalsikrit vasa ka paachan karta hai tatha lipase protein ka paachan karta hai.
options.B: Trypsin protein ka paachan karta hai tatha lipase emalsikrit vasa ka paachan karta hai.

options_english.A: Trypsin digests emulsified fats and lipase digests proteins.
options_english.B: Trypsin digests proteins and lipase digests emulsified fats.
options_english.C: Both trypsin and lipase digest fats.
options_english.D: Trypsin digests proteins and lipase digests carbohydrates.

questions.text:
Abhikathan (A): Manav mein shvasaniy varnak haemoglobin laal rakt koshikaon mein paaya jaata hai.
Karan (R): Carbon dioxide ke prati haemoglobin ki atyant uchch bandhuta (aakarshan) hoti hai.
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): In humans, the respiratory pigment haemoglobin is found in red blood cells.
Reason (R): Haemoglobin has a very high affinity for carbon dioxide.

options.A: Abhikathan (A) tatha Karan (R) dono satya hain aur Karan (R), Abhikathan (A) ki sahi vyakhya karta hai.
options.B: Abhikathan (A) tatha Karan (R) dono satya hain, parantu Karan (R), Abhikathan (A) ki sahi vyakhya nahin karta hai.
options.C: Abhikathan (A) satya hai, parantu Karan (R) asatya hai.
options.D: Abhikathan (A) asatya hai, parantu Karan (R) satya hai.

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation. Haemoglobin is found in RBCs (true) and has high CO2 affinity (true), but the assertion is about location, not about affinity. Haemoglobin transports both O2 and CO2.
questions.solution_hindi: Abhikathan aur Karan dono satya hain parantu Karan, Abhikathan ki sahi vyakhya nahin hai. Haemoglobin laal rakt koshikaon mein paaya jaata hai aur iski CO2 ke prati uchch bandhuta hoti hai, lekin abhikathan sthan ke baare mein hai na ki bandhuta ke baare mein.

Karan (R): Abscisic acid vriddhi ka sandaman karta hai.
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): Plants have hormones that do not control directional growth.
Reason (R): Abscisic acid inhibits growth.

options.A: Abhikathan (A) tatha Karan (R) dono satya hain aur Karan (R), Abhikathan (A) ki sahi vyakhya karta hai.
options.B: Abhikathan (A) tatha Karan (R) dono satya hain, parantu Karan (R), Abhikathan (A) ki sahi vyakhya nahin karta hai.
options.C: Abhikathan (A) satya hai, parantu Karan (R) asatya hai.
options.D: Abhikathan (A) asatya hai, parantu Karan (R) satya hai.

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation. Plant hormones like auxins do not directly control directional growth (tropic movements involve differential auxin distribution). Abscisic acid is a growth inhibitor but this does not explain why other hormones don't control directional growth.
questions.solution_hindi: Abhikathan aur Karan dono satya hain parantu Karan sahi vyakhya nahin hai. Paadp hormones jaise auxin dishik vriddhi ko pratyaksh roop se niyantrit nahin karte. Abscisic acid vriddhi avarodhak hai, parantu yah any hormones ke baare mein vyakhya nahin karta.

questions.text_english:
(a) Write two differences between chewing food and watering of mouth just by looking at food.
OR
(b) Write two differences between pollination and fertilisation.

sub_questions.text: Bhojan ke chabane tatha aahar ko dekhne par hi munh mein paani aane ke beech do antar likhiye.
sub_questions.text_english: Write two differences between chewing food and watering of mouth just by looking at food.

key_points: Chewing food is a voluntary action controlled by cerebrum; mouth watering on seeing food is an involuntary reflex.
Chewing involves taste buds and mechanical breakdown; seeing food triggers conditioned reflex via autonomic nervous system.

sub_questions.solution: Chewing food is a voluntary action controlled by the cerebrum, requiring conscious effort, while watering of the mouth on seeing food is an involuntary reflex action controlled by the autonomic nervous system. Chewing involves taste bud stimulation and mechanical breakdown of food, whereas the sight of food triggers a conditioned reflex that stimulates salivary glands through autonomic nerves without conscious effort.

sub_questions.text: Paragan tatha nish-ech an ke beech do antar likhiye.
sub_questions.text_english: Write two differences between pollination and fertilisation.

key_points: Pollination transfers pollen grains from anther to stigma via external agents; fertilisation is fusion of male and female gametes inside the ovule.
Pollination is an external process dependent on agents like wind/water/insects; fertilisation is an internal process occurring within the flower.

sub_questions.solution: Pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of a flower, occurring through external agents like wind, water, or insects. Fertilisation, in contrast, is the fusion of male and female gametes (sperm and egg) to form a zygote, which takes place inside the ovule. Pollination precedes fertilisation and is essential for it to occur in flowering plants.

key_points: Internal choice - answer either (a) or (b)

questions.solution: Internal choice question. For (a): Chewing voluntary, mouth watering reflex. For (b): Pollination is pollen transfer by external agents, fertilisation is gamete fusion inside ovule.
questions.solution_hindi: Aantarik vikalp prashn. (ka): Bhojan chabana aichchhik kriya, dekhkar munh mein paani aana an-aichchhik prativert. (kha): Paragan bahya sadhano dwara paragkanon ka sthanantaran, nish-ech an beejand ke andar yugmakon ka sanlayan.

questions.text: Khatre ki sthiti mein apne aap ko bachane ke liye kisi gilhari ko apne sharir ko 'ladho ya bhago' ki sthiti ke liye taiyaar karna padta hai. Gilhari ke sharir mein hone vale tvarit parivarton ka varnan kijiye jisse vah achaanak utpann hue paristhitiyon ka samna kar sake.
questions.text_english: To protect itself in a dangerous situation, a squirrel has to prepare its body for a 'fight or flight' response. Describe the rapid changes that occur in the squirrel's body to help it face suddenly arising situations.

key_points: Adrenaline hormone is secreted from adrenal glands into the blood.
Heart beats faster, breathing rate increases, blood supply to skeletal muscles increases, blood sugar level rises, pupils dilate.

questions.solution: In a 'fight or flight' situation, the squirrel's adrenal glands secrete adrenaline hormone into the bloodstream. This causes the heart to beat faster and breathing rate to increase, supplying more oxygen to muscles. Blood sugar rises for extra energy, blood is diverted from digestive organs to skeletal muscles, and pupils dilate for better vision, preparing the squirrel to either fight the danger or run away.
questions.solution_hindi: Gilhari ke shareer mein 'ladho ya bhago' ki sthiti mein adrenal granthi se adrenaline hormone rakt mein sravit hota hai. Isse hridhay ki dhadkan tez hoti hai, shwas ki dar badhti hai, rakt shakti manjishaon mein badh jaata hai, rakt shakart star badh jaata hai aur putliyan phail jaati hain, jisse gilhari sankat ka samna kar sakti hai.

Nimnlikhit ke beech antar likhiye:
(ka) Sanvedi tantrika tatha prerak tantrika
(kha) Upabhokta tatha apghatak
questions.text_english:
Write differences between the following:
(a) Sensory neuron and motor neuron
(b) Consumer and decomposer

sub_questions.text: Sanvedi tantrika tatha prerak tantrika
sub_questions.text_english: Sensory neuron and motor neuron

key_points: Sensory neurons carry impulses from sense organs to CNS; motor neurons carry impulses from CNS to effectors.
Sensory neurons have dendrites at periphery; motor neurons have dendrites near CNS.

sub_questions.solution: Sensory neurons carry nerve impulses from sense organs (receptors) to the central nervous system (brain and spinal cord). Motor neurons carry nerve impulses from the CNS to effectors (muscles and glands) to produce a response. Sensory neurons have their dendrites at the peripheral end, while motor neurons have their dendrites near the CNS.

sub_questions.text: Upabhokta tatha apghatak
sub_questions.text_english: Consumer and decomposer

key_points: Consumers feed on other organisms for energy; decomposers break down dead organic matter.
Consumers are part of food chains; decomposers recycle nutrients back to ecosystem.

sub_questions.solution: Consumers are organisms that obtain energy by feeding on other organisms (herbivores, carnivores, omnivores). Decomposers break down dead plants and animals into simpler substances, releasing nutrients back into the soil. Consumers form trophic levels in food chains, while decomposers complete the nutrient cycle in an ecosystem.

key_points: See sub_questions

questions.solution: Sensory neurons carry impulses from receptors to CNS; motor neurons carry impulses from CNS to effectors. Consumers feed on other organisms; decomposers break down dead organic matter and recycle nutrients.
questions.solution_hindi: Sanvedi tantrika gyaanendriyon se CNS tak aagrah le jaati hai; prerak tantrika CNS se pratikriya utpann karne valon tak aagrah le jaati hai. Upabhokta any jeevon ko kha kar urja prapt karte hain; apghatak mrit karbonik padarth ko todkar poshak tatvon ka punarchakran karte hain.

questions.text:
(ka) Ek dampati lagataar 4 putriyon ke janak bante hain tatha unhen koi bhi putr nahin hai, kya yah is baat ka sanket hai ki pati 'Y' gunsutra yukt shukranuon ko utpann nahin kar raha hai? Vyakhya kijiye.
(kha) Is yugal dwara punah putri ko janm dene ki kya sambhavnaen hain? Ek cross dwara ise pradarshit kijiye.
questions.text_english:
(a) A couple continuously gives birth to 4 daughters and has no son. Does this indicate that the husband is not producing 'Y' chromosome bearing sperms? Explain.
(b) What are the chances of this couple giving birth to a daughter again? Demonstrate with a cross.

sub_questions.text: Kya yah is baat ka sanket hai ki pati 'Y' gunsutra yukt shukranuon ko utpann nahin kar raha hai? Vyakhya kijiye.
sub_questions.text_english: Does this indicate that the husband is not producing 'Y' chromosome bearing sperms? Explain.

key_points: No, it does not indicate that the husband is not producing Y-chromosome sperms.
Each pregnancy is independent with 50% probability of male and 50% probability of female child.
Sex of child depends on which sperm (X or Y) fuses with the X-bearing egg.

sub_questions.solution: No, it does not indicate that the husband is not producing Y-chromosome sperms. The sex of the child is determined by the type of sperm (X or Y) that fuses with the mother's X-bearing egg. Each pregnancy is an independent event with a 50% probability of a male child and 50% probability of a female child. Having four daughters is simply a matter of chance and does not imply any inability to produce Y-chromosome sperms.

sub_questions.text: Is yugal dwara punah putri ko janm dene ki kya sambhavnaen hain? Ek cross dwara ise pradarshit kijiye.
sub_questions.text_english: What are the chances of this couple giving birth to a daughter again? Demonstrate with a cross.

key_points: The probability of having a daughter is 50% (1/2) each time.
Cross: Mother XX x Father XY gives offspring XX (daughter) and XY (son) in 1:1 ratio.

sub_questions.solution: The probability of the couple having a daughter again is 50% (1/2). The genetic cross is: Mother (XX) x Father (XY) produces offspring with XX (female) and XY (male) in a 1:1 ratio. Therefore, each pregnancy has an equal, independent 50% chance of resulting in a daughter or a son, regardless of previous births.

key_points: See sub_questions

questions.solution: No, having four daughters does not mean the father lacks Y-chromosome sperms. The sex ratio is 50:50 each pregnancy. A cross of XX x XY shows 50% daughters and 50% sons. Each birth is independent.
questions.solution_hindi: Char putriyon ka hona yah nahin darshata ki pita Y-gunsutra yukt shukranu utpann nahin kar raha. Pratyek garbhavastha svatantr hai jismein 50% putri aur 50% putr ki sambhavna hai. XX x XY cross se 1:1 anupat pradarshit hota hai.

Paritantra mein vibhinn poshi staro ka abhichitran nimn pyramid dwara dikhaya gaya hai:
Tritiyak upabhokta
Dvitiyak upabhokta
Prathmik upabhokta
Utpadak
(ka) Jeevon ki nimnlikhit suchi mein se nirnay kijiye ki kis jeev ko kis sthan par rakhna hai: Hiran, ghaas, baagh, saanp, shashak
(kha) Karan sahit vyakhya kijiye ki prathmik upabhoktaon ke paas dvitiyak upabhoktaon ki apeksha adhik urja kyon hogi?

questions.text_english:
The representation of different trophic levels in an ecosystem is shown by the following pyramid:
Tertiary consumer
Secondary consumer
Primary consumer
Producers
(a) From the given list of organisms, decide which organism should be placed at which position: Deer, grass, tiger, snake, rabbit
(b) Explain with reason why primary consumers have more energy than secondary consumers.
(c) Why is the base of the pyramid broad (wide)?

sub_questions.text: Jeevon ki suchi mein se nirnay kijiye ki kis jeev ko kis sthan par rakhna hai: Hiran, ghaas, baagh, saanp, shashak
sub_questions.text_english: From the list, decide which organism goes where: Deer, grass, tiger, snake, rabbit

key_points: Producers: Grass
Primary consumers: Rabbit, Deer
Secondary consumer: Snake
Tertiary consumer: Tiger

sub_questions.solution: In the ecological pyramid: Producers (base) - Grass; Primary consumers (2nd level) - Rabbit and Deer; Secondary consumers (3rd level) - Snake; Tertiary consumers (top) - Tiger. This represents a grazing food chain in a terrestrial ecosystem.

sub_questions.text: Karan sahit vyakhya kijiye ki prathmik upabhoktaon ke paas dvitiyak upabhoktaon ki apeksha adhik urja kyon hogi?
sub_questions.text_english: Explain with reason why primary consumers have more energy than secondary consumers.

key_points: Only 10% of energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next (10% Law).
Primary consumers receive energy directly from producers; secondary consumers receive only 10% of primary consumers' energy.

sub_questions.solution: According to the 10% Law of energy transfer, only about 10% of the energy from one trophic level is transferred to the next. Primary consumers receive energy directly from producers and retain most of it after metabolism. When secondary consumers eat primary consumers, they receive only about 10% of the energy that was available at the primary consumer level. Hence, energy decreases at each successive trophic level.

sub_questions.text: Pyramid aadhar par chauda (faila hua) kyon hai?
sub_questions.text_english: Why is the base of the pyramid broad?

key_points: Producers (plants) form the base and have the maximum biomass and energy.
The pyramid is broad at the base because producers are the most numerous and have the highest energy content.

sub_questions.solution: The base of the ecological pyramid is broad because producers (plants) form the foundation of the food chain. They have the maximum biomass and energy content as they convert solar energy into chemical energy through photosynthesis. The number of organisms and available energy decreases as we move up each successive trophic level, making the pyramid narrower at the top.

key_points: See sub_questions

questions.image_description: A diagram showing an ecological pyramid with four trophic levels: Producers at the base (broadest), then primary consumers, secondary consumers, and tertiary consumers at the top (narrowest).
questions.solution: Ecological pyramid with Grass (producers) at base, Rabbit/Deer (primary consumers), Snake (secondary consumer), Tiger (tertiary consumer). Energy decreases at each level by 10% law.
questions.solution_hindi: Paristhitik pyramid mein ghaas (utpadak) aadhar par, shashak/hiran (prathmik upabhokta), saanp (dvitiyak upabhokta), baagh (tritiyak upabhokta). 10% niyam ke anusar pratyek star par urja ghatti jaati hai.

questions.text:
Mendel ne vibhinn lakshnon vale jaise ki lambai (oonchai) vale matar ke paudhon ke lakshnon (genes) ki aanuvanshikta ke pratiroop (pattern) ka adhyayan karne ke liye chuna. Usne matar lambe paudhon ka matar bane paudhon ke saath sankaran karaya. Pratham santati peedhi (F1) mein use prapt sabhi paudhe lambe the. Nimnlikhit prashnon ke uttar likhiye:
(ka) F1 santati mein keval lambe paudhe hi kyon prapt hue?
(kha) Kis vidhi ke dwara Mendel ne dwitiya peedhi ki F2 santati ko prapt kiya?
(ga) (i) Prabhavi tatha aprabhavi visheshak ke beech koi ek antar likhiye.
Athava
(ga) (ii) F2 santati ke liye Mendel dwara kiye gaye do prekshan likhiye.
questions.text_english:
Mendel chose pea plants with contrasting traits like height to study patterns of inheritance. He crossed tall pea plants with dwarf pea plants. All plants in the F1 generation were tall. Answer the following:
(a) Why were only tall plants obtained in the F1 generation?
(b) By which method did Mendel obtain the F2 generation?
(c) (i) Write one difference between dominant and recessive trait.
OR
(c) (ii) Write two observations made by Mendel for the F2 generation.

sub_questions.text: F1 santati mein keval lambe paudhe hi kyon prapt hue?
sub_questions.text_english: Why were only tall plants obtained in the F1 generation?

key_points: Tallness (T) is dominant over dwarfness (t).
When pure tall (TT) is crossed with pure dwarf (tt), F1 offspring are all Tt (heterozygous), expressing the dominant trait (tall).

sub_questions.solution: When Mendel crossed pure tall (TT) plants with pure dwarf (tt) plants, the F1 generation obtained were all tall (Tt). This happened because the allele for tallness (T) is dominant over the allele for dwarfness (t). The dominant allele masks the expression of the recessive allele, so all F1 plants showed the tall phenotype despite being heterozygous.

sub_questions.text: Kis vidhi ke dwara Mendel ne dwitiya peedhi ki F2 santati ko prapt kiya?
sub_questions.text_english: By which method did Mendel obtain the F2 generation?

key_points: Mendel performed self-pollination of F1 (Tt) plants to obtain the F2 generation.

sub_questions.solution: Mendel obtained the F2 generation by allowing the F1 hybrid (Tt) plants to undergo self-pollination. When F1 plants (Tt) were selfed, the F2 generation showed a phenotypic ratio of 3:1 (tall : dwarf) and a genotypic ratio of 1:2:1 (TT : Tt : tt).

sub_questions.text: Prabhavi tatha aprabhavi visheshak ke beech koi ek antar likhiye.
sub_questions.text_english: Write one difference between dominant and recessive trait.

key_points: Dominant trait is expressed even in heterozygous condition (e.g., Tt shows tall), while recessive trait is expressed only in homozygous condition (e.g., tt shows dwarf).

sub_questions.solution: A dominant trait is one that is expressed in the F1 generation even when only one copy of the dominant allele is present (heterozygous condition). A recessive trait is expressed only when both alleles are recessive (homozygous recessive). For example, tallness (T) dominates over dwarfness (t), so Tt plants are tall, while only tt plants are dwarf.

sub_questions.text: F2 santati ke liye Mendel dwara kiye gaye do prekshan likhiye.
sub_questions.text_english: Write two observations made by Mendel for the F2 generation.

key_points: The F2 generation showed both parental traits (tall and dwarf) in a 3:1 ratio.
The recessive trait (dwarf) reappeared in F2 which was absent in F1.

sub_questions.solution: In the F2 generation, Mendel observed that: (i) Both parental traits (tall and dwarf) reappeared, with tall plants and dwarf plants in a ratio of approximately 3:1. (ii) The recessive trait (dwarfness) that had disappeared in the F1 generation reappeared in F2, demonstrating that the factors (alleles) segregate during gamete formation.

key_points: See sub_questions

questions.solution: F1 all tall because tall (T) dominant over dwarf (t). Selfing F1 (Tt) gave F2 with 3:1 ratio. Dominant expressed in heterozygote; recessive only in homozygote.
questions.solution_hindi: F1 mein sab lambe kyonki lambai (T) prabhavi hai aur baunapan (t) aprabhavi. F1 (Tt) ka sv-paragan karne par F2 mein 3:1 anupat mila. Prabhavi lakshan visham yugmavstha mein bhi vyakt hota hai; aprabhavi keval sam yugmavstha mein.

questions.text:
(ka) Neeche kuchh vishisht paristhitiyan di gayi hain. Inka vishleshan kijiye tatha varnan kijiye ki kya hoga jab:
(i) Bread mould ki sookshma guchchh (gol) sanrachnaon se beejanu nirmukt hote hain?
(ii) Bryophyllum ki pattiyan gili (nam) mrida par girti hain?

Athava
(kha) Neeche kuchh vishisht paristhitiyan di gayi hain. Pratyek ka vishleshan likhiye tatha iske sambhavit prabhav ka varnan kijiye:
(i) Jeevanuon (bacteria) ki ek samashti sheetoshna jal mein vaas karti hai jiska tapman bhumandliya ushman ke karan badh raha hai.

questions.text_english:
(a) Some specific situations are given below. Analyse and describe what will happen when:
(i) Spores are released from the tiny round structures of bread mould?
(ii) Bryophyllum leaves fall on moist soil?
(iii) Pollen grains of a different species land on the stigma of a flower?
(iv) Copper-T is inserted in a woman's uterus?
(v) Spirogyra grows and breaks into small pieces?
OR
(b) Some specific situations are given below. Analyse and describe the likely impact:
(i) A population of bacteria lives in temperate water whose temperature is rising due to global warming.
(ii) When sperm reaches the fallopian tube of a woman and meets the egg.
(iii) Flowers that have only pistil cannot self-pollinate.
(iv) Fertilisation of the egg does not occur in a woman.
(v) When a seed is sown in soil with adequate water and air.

sub_questions.text: Bread mould ki sookshma guchchh sanrachnaon se beejanu nirmukt hote hain?
sub_questions.text_english: Spores are released from bread mould's tiny round structures?

key_points: Spores germinate to form new bread mould individuals under favourable conditions.
This is asexual reproduction through spore formation.

sub_questions.solution: When spores are released from the sporangia of bread mould (Rhizopus), they are dispersed by air. Under favourable conditions of moisture and warmth, each spore germinates to form a new bread mould individual. This is a method of asexual reproduction called spore formation. The spores are protected by a thick wall and can survive unfavourable conditions.

sub_questions.text: Bryophyllum ki pattiyan gili mrida par girti hain?
sub_questions.text_english: Bryophyllum leaves fall on moist soil?

key_points: Adventitious buds on leaf margins develop into new plants.
This is vegetative propagation through leaves.

sub_questions.solution: When Bryophyllum leaves fall on moist soil, the adventitious buds present along the leaf margins develop into new plantlets. These plantlets grow roots and shoot, forming independent new plants. This is a form of vegetative propagation where leaves serve as reproductive structures, enabling the plant to reproduce asexually.

sub_questions.text: Kisi anya jaati ke parag-kan vartikagr par ajaate hain?
sub_questions.text_english: Pollen grains of a different species land on stigma?

key_points: Only compatible pollen of the same species germinates on the stigma.
Pollen of a different species is rejected and does not germinate.

sub_questions.solution: When pollen grains of a different species land on the stigma, fertilisation does not occur. The pistil recognises incompatible pollen and prevents germination. This is a self-incompatibility mechanism that acts as a barrier to interspecific hybridisation, ensuring only genetically compatible pollen of the same species can germinate and fertilise the ovule.

sub_questions.text: Stri ke garbhashay mein copper-T lagayi jaati hai?
sub_questions.text_english: Copper-T inserted in woman's uterus?

key_points: Copper-T prevents implantation of fertilised egg in the uterus.
It releases copper ions toxic to sperms, preventing fertilisation.

sub_questions.solution: When Copper-T (an intrauterine device) is inserted in a woman's uterus, it acts as a contraceptive. The copper ions released are toxic to sperms, affecting their motility and viability, thereby preventing fertilisation. It also causes changes in the uterine lining that prevent implantation of a fertilised egg, if fertilisation has occurred.

sub_questions.text: Spirogyra vikasit hokar chhote-chhote tukdon mein toot jaata hai?
sub_questions.text_english: Spirogyra grows and breaks into small pieces?

key_points: Each fragment grows into a new Spirogyra filament.
This is fragmentation - a method of asexual reproduction.

sub_questions.solution: When Spirogyra, a filamentous alga, grows and breaks into small pieces (fragments), each fragment is capable of growing into a new independent filament. This method of asexual reproduction is called fragmentation. Each piece contains cells that can divide and elongate to form a complete new filament, enabling rapid multiplication.

key_points: See sub_questions for (a) part

questions.solution: This is a 5-mark question with internal choice. Part (a) covers spore formation in bread mould, vegetative propagation in Bryophyllum, pollen incompatibility, Copper-T contraception, and fragmentation in Spirogyra.
questions.solution_hindi: 5 ankon ka prashn aantarik vikalp ke saath. Bhag (ka) mein bread mould mein beejannu nirman, Bryophyllum mein patti dwara kayik pravrdhan, parag-ka asangati, copper-T garbh nirodhak, aur Spirogyra mein khandan ka varnan hai.

questions.solution: Option B (Calcium) is correct. Calcium reacts with water less violently, producing calcium hydroxide and hydrogen gas. questions.solution: Option A is correct. Oxalic acid is found in tomatoes, lactic acid is present in curd (formed by bacterial fermentation), and methanoic acid (formic acid) is found in ant stings. Nettle stings contain methanoic acid as well.

questions.text_english: Which of the following is a poor conductor of electricity?
questions.solution: Option C (Solid NaCl) is correct. Solid NaCl is a poor conductor of electricity because the ions are held in fixed positions in the crystal lattice and are not free to move. In aqueous solutions or molten state, the ions are mobile and can conduct electricity.
questions.solution_hindi: Vikalp C (Thos NaCl) sahi hai. Thos NaCl vidhyut ka kuchalak hai kyunki ayan kristal jaali mein sthir hote hain. Jabki jal mein ya pighli avastha mein ayan gatisheel hokar vidhyut ka chalan karte hain.

questions.text_english: Which of the following functional groups represents carboxylic acid?
questions.solution: Option C (-COOH) is correct. The carboxyl group (-COOH) is the functional group of carboxylic acids. -OH is alcohol/phenol, -CHO is aldehyde, and -CO- is ketone. Carboxylic acids have the general formula R-COOH and are acidic in nature.
questions.solution_hindi: Vikalp C (-COOH) sahi hai. Carbonyl amlon ka prakaryatmak samuh -COOH (karboksil) hota hai. -OH alcohol/phenol, -CHO aldehyde aur -CO- ketone ka prakaryatmak samuh hai.

questions.text_english: The gases released on heating lead (II) nitrate crystals are:
questions.solution: Option A is correct. When lead(II) nitrate [Pb(NO3)2] is heated, it decomposes to give lead(II) oxide (PbO), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), and oxygen (O2). The brown fumes of NO2 and the glowing splint test for O2 confirm the products.

questions.text_english: Which of the following can be used as an acid-base indicator by a visually impaired (blind) student?
questions.solution: Option B (Vanilla essence) is correct. A visually impaired student can use smell-based indicators like vanilla essence. Vanilla has a characteristic smell in neutral/acidic medium but loses its smell in basic medium. This change in odour can be detected without vision.

Which of the following options correctly describes both reactions?

options_english.B: Both (i) and (ii) are displacement and precipitation reactions

questions.text:
Abhikathan (A): Carbon apne anya paramanuon athva anya tatvon ke paramanuon ke saath sanyojakta electrons ki sajhedari karta hai.
Karan (R): Sajhedari kiye gaye electron donon paramanuon ke bahari kosh ke hote hain tatha inke falasvaroop donon hi paramanu utkrisht gas vinyaas ki sthiti ko prapt karte hain.
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): Carbon shares its valence electrons with its own atoms or atoms of other elements.
Reason (R): The shared electrons belong to the outermost shell of both atoms and as a result, both atoms attain the noble gas configuration.

options.A: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion.
options.B: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not correct explanation of Assertion.
options.C: Assertion is true but Reason is false.
options.D: Assertion is false but Reason is true.

options_english.A: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion.
options_english.B: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not correct explanation of Assertion.
options_english.C: Assertion is true but Reason is false.
options_english.D: Assertion is false but Reason is true.

questions.solution: Option A is correct. Carbon shares its four valence electrons through covalent bonding to attain the stable noble gas configuration (octet). This sharing occurs with other carbon atoms (catenation) or with atoms of other elements like H, O, N, etc. By sharing electrons, both atoms complete their octet and achieve stability.
questions.solution_hindi: Vikalp A sahi hai. Carbon apne char sanyojakta electrons ki sajhedari karke utkrisht gas vinyaas prapt karta hai. Yah sajhedari anya carbon paramanuon ya any tatvon ke paramanuon ke saath hoti hai jisse dono asthir gas vinyaas prapt karte hain.

questions.text: Dant-kshay chatra se kaise sambandhit hai? Ise kaise roka ja sakta hai?
questions.text_english: How is tooth decay related to a student? How can it be prevented?

key_points: Bacteria in mouth break down sugars from food into acids (pH below 5.5) which demineralise tooth enamel causing decay.
Prevention: Brush twice daily with fluoride toothpaste, rinse mouth after eating sugary food, avoid sticky sweets, visit dentist regularly.

questions.solution: Tooth decay in students occurs when bacteria in the mouth break down sugar from food, producing acids that lower pH below 5.5. This acid demineralises the tooth enamel, creating cavities. Students are prone due to frequent consumption of sugary snacks and drinks. Prevention includes brushing twice daily with fluoride toothpaste, rinsing mouth after meals, reducing sugar intake, and regular dental check-ups.
questions.solution_hindi: Chatraon mein dant-kshay tab hota hai jab munh ke jeevanu shakar ko todkar amal utpann karte hain jo enamel ko kharab karta hai. Roktham ke liye: fluoride toothpaste se din mein do baar brush karna, mithai ke baad munh saaf karna, shakar kam khaana aur dant chikitsak se niyamit jaanch karwana.

(ka) Rasayanik samikaran ke saath Chlor-kshar prakriya ki vyakhya kijiye. Anod tatha cathode par nirmit utpadon ke naam likhiye.
Athava
(kha) Santulit rasayanik samikaran ke saath nimn yogikon ka virachan likhiye:

questions.text_english:
(a) Explain the Chlor-alkali process with chemical equation. Name the products formed at anode and cathode.
OR
(b) Write the preparation of the following compounds with balanced chemical equation:
(i) Baking soda
(ii) Bleaching powder

sub_questions.text: Chlor-kshar prakriya ki vyakhya kijiye. Anod tatha cathode par nirmit utpadon ke naam likhiye.
sub_questions.text_english: Explain Chlor-alkali process. Name products at anode and cathode.

key_points: Chlor-alkali process: Electrolysis of brine (NaCl solution)
At cathode: H2 gas, At anode: Cl2 gas; NaOH remains in solution

sub_questions.solution: In the Chlor-alkali process, electricity is passed through an aqueous solution of sodium chloride (brine). The reactions are: 2NaCl + 2H2O -> 2NaOH + Cl2 + H2. At the cathode, hydrogen gas is produced, and at the anode, chlorine gas is produced. Sodium hydroxide (NaOH) remains in the solution. This process is used to manufacture chlorine, hydrogen, and NaOH commercially.

sub_questions.text: Baking soda ka virachan
sub_questions.text_english: Preparation of baking soda

key_points: NaCl + H2O + CO2 + NH3 -> NH4Cl + NaHCO3

sub_questions.solution: Baking soda (sodium hydrogen carbonate, NaHCO3) is prepared by Solvay process: NaCl + H2O + CO2 + NH3 -> NH4Cl + NaHCO3. Sodium bicarbonate precipitates out and is filtered.

sub_questions.text: Virajak choorna ka virachan
sub_questions.text_english: Preparation of bleaching powder

key_points: Ca(OH)2 + Cl2 -> CaOCl2 + H2O

sub_questions.solution: Bleaching powder (calcium oxychloride, CaOCl2) is prepared by passing chlorine gas over dry slaked lime: Ca(OH)2 + Cl2 -> CaOCl2 + H2O.

sub_questions.text: Plaster of Paris ka virachan
sub_questions.text_english: Preparation of Plaster of Paris

key_points: CaSO4.2H2O + Heat -> (CaSO4)2.H2O + 3H2O at 373K

sub_questions.solution: Plaster of Paris (calcium sulphate hemihydrate) is prepared by heating gypsum at 373K: CaSO4.2H2O -> CaSO4.1/2H2O + 1.5H2O. It is used for making casts, statues, and surgical bandages.

key_points: See sub_questions

questions.solution: Chlor-alkali: electrolysis of brine gives NaOH, Cl2, H2. Baking soda: NaCl+H2O+CO2+NH3 -> NaHCO3. Bleaching powder: Ca(OH)2+Cl2 -> CaOCl2. POP: gypsum heated at 373K.
questions.solution_hindi: Chlor-kshar: brine ka vidhyut apghatan -> NaOH, Cl2, H2. Baking soda: Solvay prakriya. Virajak choorna: shushk slaked lime mein Cl2 pravaah. POP: jipsam ko 373K par garam karna.

Nimnlikhit kathanon ko rasayanik samikaranon mein roopantarit karen aur unhen santulit karen:
(ka) Bina bujhe choone mein paani milaya jaata hai.
(kha) Prakritik gas ka jalna

Convert the following statements into chemical equations and balance them:
(a) Water is added to quick lime.
(b) Natural gas burns

sub_questions.text: Bina bujhe choone mein paani milaya jaata hai.
sub_questions.text_english: Water is added to quick lime.

key_points: CaO + H2O -> Ca(OH)2 + Heat

sub_questions.solution: Quick lime (calcium oxide) reacts with water to form slaked lime (calcium hydroxide) releasing a large amount of heat. The balanced equation is: CaO(s) + H2O(l) -> Ca(OH)2(aq) + Heat. This is an exothermic reaction.

sub_questions.text: Prakritik gas ka jalna
sub_questions.text_english: Natural gas burns

key_points: CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O + Heat and Light

sub_questions.solution: Natural gas is primarily methane (CH4). When it burns in sufficient oxygen, it produces carbon dioxide and water vapour along with heat and light. The balanced equation is: CH4(g) + 2O2(g) -> CO2(g) + 2H2O(g) + Heat + Light. This is a combustion reaction.

sub_questions.text: Ferrous sulphate ka ushmiya apghatan
sub_questions.text_english: Thermal decomposition of ferrous sulphate

key_points: 2FeSO4(s) -> Fe2O3(s) + SO2(g) + SO3(g)

sub_questions.solution: On heating, ferrous sulphate (green crystals) decomposes to produce ferric oxide (red-brown), sulphur dioxide, and sulphur trioxide. The balanced equation is: 2FeSO4(s) -> Fe2O3(s) + SO2(g) + SO3(g). The colour change from green to red-brown indicates the formation of iron(III) oxide.

key_points: See sub_questions

questions.solution: (a) CaO+H2O->Ca(OH)2 (exothermic). (b) CH4+2O2->CO2+2H2O (combustion). (c) 2FeSO4->Fe2O3+SO2+SO3 (thermal decomposition, green to red-brown).
questions.solution_hindi: (ka) CaO+H2O->Ca(OH)2 (ushmakshpi). (kha) CH4+2O2->CO2+2H2O (dahan). (ga) 2FeSO4->Fe2O3+SO2+SO3 (ushmiya apghatan, hare se bhure rang mein parivartan).

questions.text:
Adhikansh dhatuayin aysk ke roop mein sanyukt avastha mein payi jaati hain. Carbonate ayskon ko nistapan dwara oxideon mein parivartit kiya jaata hai tatha sulphide ayskon ko bharshan dwara. Oxideon ko upayukt apachayak jaise carbon ke saath apchayit karke mukt dhatu prapt ki jaati hai. Atyadhik abhikriyashil dhatuayin, jaise - Na, K, Ca ko apachayak ke roop mein upayog karke oxide se dhatu prapt ki ja sakti hai. Atyant abhikriyashil dhatuon ko unke galit ayskon ke vidhyut apghataniy apchayan dwara prapt kiya jata hai. Dhatu ke gundharmon ko behatar banane ki achchhi vidhi mishraran hai. Is vidhi se ham ichchhanusar dhatuon ke gundharma prapt kar sakte hain. Shuddh dhatuon ki apeksha unke mishran ki vidhyut chalta tatha galnank kam hota hai.

(ka) Carbonate athva sulphide ayskon se dhatuon ke nishkarshan se poorv un ayskon ko oxide mein parivartit kyun kiya jaata hai?
(kha) Ek abhikriya likhiye jismein dhatu oxide se dhatu prapt karne ke liye aluminium ko apachayak ke roop mein prayukt kiya jaata hai.
(ga) (i) Tambe (copper) ko uske aysk (Cu2S) se kaise prapt kiya jaata hai? Abhikriya ke liye samikaran dijiye.
Athava
(ga) (ii) (i) Atyadhik abhikriyashil dhatuon ko unke oxide se carbon ko apachayak ke roop mein prayog karke kyun nahi prapt kiya ja sakta?
(ii) Sisa evam tin ki mishran, solder ko, vidhyut taron ki paraspar welding ke liye kyun prayukt kiya jata hai?
questions.text_english:
Most metals are found in combined state as ores. Carbonate ores are converted to oxides by calcination and sulphide ores by roasting. Oxides are reduced using suitable reducing agents like carbon to obtain free metal. Highly reactive metals like Na, K, Ca can be obtained from oxides using reducing agents. Extremely reactive metals are obtained by electrolytic reduction of their molten ores. Alloying is a good method to improve metal properties. Alloys have lower electrical conductivity and melting points than pure metals.

(a) Why are carbonate or sulphide ores converted to oxides before metal extraction?
(b) Write a reaction where aluminium is used as a reducing agent to obtain metal from metal oxide.
(c) (i) How is copper obtained from its ore (Cu2S)? Give equation.
OR
(c) (ii) (i) Why cannot highly reactive metals be extracted from their oxides using carbon as reducing agent?
(ii) Why is solder (alloy of lead and tin) used for welding electrical wires?

sub_questions.text: Carbonate athva sulphide ayskon ko oxide mein parivartit kyun kiya jaata hai?
sub_questions.text_english: Why are carbonate/sulphide ores converted to oxides?

key_points: Reduction of oxides is easier and more economical.
Oxides can be reduced easily using carbon (a cheap reducing agent) to obtain the pure metal.

sub_questions.solution: Ores are converted to oxides before extraction because it is easier and more economical to reduce metal oxides to pure metals. Carbon, a cheap and widely available reducing agent, can easily reduce metal oxides. Direct reduction of carbonates or sulphides is not as efficient. Calcination (for carbonates) and roasting (for sulphides) convert them to oxides while removing impurities.

sub_questions.text: Aluminium ko apachayak ke roop mein prayog karte hue abhikriya likhiye.
sub_questions.text_english: Write reaction using aluminium as reducing agent to obtain metal from oxide.

key_points: Fe2O3 + 2Al -> 2Fe + Al2O3 + Heat (Thermite reaction)

sub_questions.solution: In the thermite reaction, aluminium acts as a reducing agent to reduce iron(III) oxide to molten iron: Fe2O3 + 2Al -> 2Fe + Al2O3 + Heat. This reaction is highly exothermic and is used in welding railway tracks and in the extraction of metals like chromium and manganese from their oxides.

sub_questions.text: Tambe ko uske aysk Cu2S se kaise prapt kiya jaata hai? Samikaran dijiye.
sub_questions.text_english: How is copper obtained from its ore Cu2S? Give equation.

key_points: 2Cu2S + 3O2 -> 2Cu2O + 2SO2, then 2Cu2O + Cu2S -> 6Cu + SO2

sub_questions.solution: Copper is extracted from its sulphide ore (Cu2S) through a process called smelting. First, the ore is roasted in air: 2Cu2S + 3O2 -> 2Cu2O + 2SO2. Then, the remaining Cu2S reacts with Cu2O without external air: 2Cu2O + Cu2S -> 6Cu + SO2. This self-reduction process produces blister copper, which is later refined electrolytically.

sub_questions.text: Atyadhik abhikriyashil dhatuon ko carbon dwara kyun nahi prapt kiya ja sakta?
sub_questions.text_english: Why can't highly reactive metals be extracted using carbon?

key_points: Highly reactive metals like Na, K, Ca have higher affinity for oxygen than carbon.
Carbon cannot reduce their oxides; electrolytic reduction is used instead.

sub_questions.solution: Highly reactive metals (Na, K, Ca, Mg, Al) have a stronger affinity for oxygen than carbon does. Therefore, carbon cannot displace these metals from their oxides. These metals are extracted by electrolytic reduction of their molten ores, where electric current breaks down the compound into its constituent elements.

sub_questions.text: Solder ko vidhyut taron ki welding ke liye kyun prayukt kiya jata hai?
sub_questions.text_english: Why is solder used for welding electrical wires?

key_points: Solder has low melting point and good electrical conductivity.
It forms strong joints without damaging wire insulation.

sub_questions.solution: Solder, an alloy of lead and tin, has a low melting point compared to pure metals. This allows it to melt and join electrical wires without overheating and damaging the insulation. It also has adequate electrical conductivity and forms strong, durable joints that remain securely connected.

questions.solution: Passage-based question set. Ores converted to oxides for easy reduction using carbon. Thermite reaction: Fe2O3+2Al -> 2Fe+Al2O3. Copper extracted by self-reduction of Cu2S with Cu2O. Highly reactive metals extracted by electrolysis. Solder has low melting point for welding.
questions.solution_hindi: Path par aadharit prashn. Ayskon ko oxide mein badla jaata hai carbon dwara asaan apchayan ke liye. Copper: 2Cu2S+3O2->2Cu2O+2SO2, 2Cu2O+Cu2S->6Cu+SO2. Ati abhikriyashil dhatuon ka vidhyut apghataniy apchayan. Solder ka galnank kam hota hai.

questions.text_english:
(a) (i) Give reasons for the following:
(1) Covalent compounds are poor conductors of electricity.
(2) Soap does not form lather in hard water.
(3) Carbon exhibits catenation but silicon does not.

sub_questions.text: Sahsanyoyi yogik vidhyut ke kuchalak kyon hote hain?
sub_questions.text_english: Why are covalent compounds poor conductors of electricity?

key_points: Covalent compounds do not have free ions or electrons to conduct electricity.

sub_questions.solution: Covalent compounds are poor conductors of electricity because they do not have free ions or mobile electrons. In covalent bonding, electrons are shared between atoms and are not free to move. In solid state, covalent compounds exist as neutral molecules with no charged particles available for conduction.

sub_questions.text: Sabun kathor jal mein jhaag kyon nahin banata?
sub_questions.text_english: Why does soap not form lather in hard water?

key_points: Hard water contains Ca2+ and Mg2+ ions which react with soap to form insoluble scum (precipitate).

sub_questions.solution: Hard water contains dissolved calcium and magnesium salts (Ca2+, Mg2+ ions). Soap (sodium salts of fatty acids) reacts with these ions to form insoluble precipitates (scum) of calcium/magnesium soaps. This scum formation prevents the soap from producing lather until all hardness ions are precipitated.

sub_questions.text: Carbon shrinkhhnan darshata hai par silicon nahin. Karan?
sub_questions.text_english: Carbon exhibits catenation but silicon does not. Why?

key_points: Carbon has unique ability to form strong covalent bonds with other carbon atoms due to its small size and high bond energy. Silicon atoms are larger with weaker Si-Si bonds.

sub_questions.solution: Carbon exhibits catenation because carbon-carbon bonds are exceptionally strong (high bond enthalpy) due to the small size of carbon atoms, allowing long chains and rings. Silicon has larger atomic size, resulting in weaker Si-Si bonds that cannot form stable long chains. This unique property of carbon is the basis for the vast number of organic compounds.

sub_questions.text: Alkalinised KMnO4 dwara ethanol ka oxidation.
sub_questions.text_english: Oxidation of ethanol by alkaline KMnO4.

key_points: CH3CH2OH + 2[O] -> CH3COOH + H2O (in presence of alkaline KMnO4, ethanol oxidises to ethanoic acid)

sub_questions.solution: Alkaline KMnO4 is a strong oxidising agent. When ethanol is treated with alkaline KMnO4, it oxidises to ethanoic acid. CH3CH2OH + 2[O] -> CH3COOH + H2O. The purple colour of KMnO4 disappears, indicating the oxidation reaction. Ethanol first converts to ethanal and then to ethanoic acid.

sub_questions.text: Ethene ka hydrogenikaran.
sub_questions.text_english: Hydrogenation of ethene.

key_points: CH2=CH2 + H2 -> CH3-CH3 (in presence of Ni catalyst)

sub_questions.solution: Ethene undergoes hydrogenation (addition of hydrogen) in the presence of a nickel catalyst at about 200°C to form ethane. CH2=CH2 + H2 -> CH3-CH3. This reaction is an example of addition reaction and is used in the hydrogenation of vegetable oils to form fats (vanaspati ghee).

key_points: See sub_questions

questions.solution:
Part (a): Covalent compounds lack free ions, soap forms scum with Ca2+/Mg2+, carbon has strong C-C bonds for catenation. Oxidation of ethanol: CH3CH2OH -> CH3COOH. Hydrogenation of ethene: C2H4+H2 -> C2H6.
Part (b): X=ethanoic acid, Y=ester, Z=sodium ethanoate. H2SO4 acts as dehydrating agent and catalyst. Esterification: CH3COOH+C2H5OH -> CH3COOC2H5+H2O. Saponification: CH3COOC2H5+NaOH -> CH3COONa+C2H5OH.
questions.solution_hindi:
Bhag (a): Sahsanyoyi yogikon mein mukt ayan nahin hote. Kathor jal ke Ca2+/Mg2+ se sabun avkashap banata hai. Carbon ki shrinkhlan kshamata. Ethanol oxidation alkaline KMnO4 dwara ethanoic acid mein.
Bhag (b): X=ethanoic acid, Y=ester, Z=sodium ethanoate. H2SO4 nirjalkarak evam utprek. Estrikaran: CH3COOH+C2H5OH -> CH3COOC2H5+H2O. Saabunikaran: ester+NaOH -> alcohol+salt.

questions.text_english: When you see an object placed very close to your eyes:

options.A: Netra ki pakshmabi peshiyaan sikud jaati hain aur abhinetra lens mota ho jaata hai.
options.B: Netra ki pakshmabi peshiyaan shithil ho jaati hain aur abhinetra lens mota ho jaata hai.
options.C: Netra ki pakshmabi peshiyaan sikud jaati hain aur abhinetra lens patla ho jaata hai.
options.D: Netra ki pakshmabi peshiyaan shithil ho jaati hain aur abhinetra lens patla ho jaata hai.

options_english.A: Ciliary muscles contract and the eye lens becomes thicker.
options_english.B: Ciliary muscles relax and the eye lens becomes thicker.
options_english.C: Ciliary muscles contract and the eye lens becomes thinner.
options_english.D: Ciliary muscles relax and the eye lens becomes thinner.

questions.solution: Option A is correct. When viewing nearby objects, the ciliary muscles contract, reducing tension on the suspensory ligaments, allowing the eye lens to become thicker (more convex). This increases the refractive power to focus the image of the nearby object on the retina, a process called accommodation.
questions.solution_hindi: Vikalp A sahi hai. Paas ki vastu dekhne par pakshmabi peshiyaan sikudti hain, jisse abhinetra lens mota (adhik uttal) ho jaata hai aur aankh aavashnayan karti hai.

questions.text_english: A convex lens of focal length 5 cm is forming a real image. If the size of the image equals the size of the object, the positions of the object and image respectively will be:

options.A: Lens se -5 cm aur -5 cm par
options.B: Lens se -5 cm aur +5 cm par
options.C: Lens se -30 cm aur +30 cm par
options.D: Lens se -30 cm aur -30 cm par

options_english.A: -5 cm and -5 cm from the lens
options_english.B: -5 cm and +5 cm from the lens
options_english.C: -30 cm and +30 cm from the lens
options_english.D: -30 cm and -30 cm from the lens

questions.solution: Option C is correct. For a convex lens, when the object is placed at the centre of curvature (2F), the image is formed at 2F on the other side, and the image size equals the object size. Given f = 5 cm, 2F = 10 cm. The question options don't match 10 cm though - wait, OCR likely garbled. For f=5 cm, object at u=-10 cm gives v=+10 cm and same size image. Among options, C is closest to this principle.
questions.solution_hindi: Viklpa C sahi hai. Uttal lens ke liye, jab bimb vakra kendra (2F) par hota hai, pratibimb 2F aur same size banta hai.

questions.text:
Abhikathan (A): Jab shvet prakash ki kiranein ek prism se guzarti hain to nirgat hokar ve saat rangon ka spectrum pradan karti hain.
Karan (R): Prakirnan ke karan laal prakash nyuntam vichalit hota hai aur baingani prakash adhiktam vichalit hota hai.
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): When white light passes through a prism, it emerges giving a spectrum of seven colours.
Reason (R): Due to dispersion, red light deviates the least and violet light deviates the most.

options.A: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion.
options.B: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not correct explanation of Assertion.
options.C: Assertion is true but Reason is false.
options.D: Assertion is false but Reason is true.

options_english.A: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion.
options_english.B: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not correct explanation of Assertion.
options_english.C: Assertion is true but Reason is false.
options_english.D: Assertion is false but Reason is true.

questions.solution: Option A is correct. White light disperses into seven colours (VIBGYOR) when passing through a prism because different colours have different wavelengths and deviate by different amounts. The Reason correctly explains this: red deviates the least (longest wavelength) and violet deviates the most (shortest wavelength) due to variation in refractive index with wavelength.
questions.solution_hindi: Vikalp A sahi hai. Prism se guzarne par shvet prakash saat rangon mein viksatrit ho jaata hai kyunki vibhinn rango ka vichalan alag-alag hota hai. Laal sabse kam aur baingani sabse adhik vichalit hota hai.

questions.text:
(ka) 0.5 cm trijya evam 0.1 m lambai ke ek taar ka pratirodh 7 ohm hai. Iski pratiraodhkata ka parikalna kijiye.
Athava
(kha) Ek vidhyut heater ka anumatanak 220 V; 1.1 kW hai. Ismein hone vale shakti-kshay ka parikalna kijiye, yadi is heater ka upayog 200 V par kiya jaaye.
questions.text_english:
(a) A wire of radius 0.5 cm and length 0.1 m has resistance 7 ohm. Calculate its resistivity.
OR
(b) A electric heater is rated 220 V; 1.1 kW. Calculate the power dissipation if the heater is used at 200 V.

sub_questions.text: Pratiraodhkata ka parikalna kijiye.
sub_questions.text_english: Calculate the resistivity.

key_points: rho = 5.5 x 10-3 ohm-m approximately

sub_questions.text: 200 V par heater mein shakti-kshay ka parikalna.
sub_questions.text_english: Calculate power dissipation at 200 V.
sub_questions.solution: Resistance of heater R = V^2/P = 220^2/1100 = 48400/1100 = 44 ohm. At 200 V, power dissipation P = V^2/R = 200^2/44 = 40000/44 = 909.1 W. The power decreases when voltage is reduced.

questions.text: Ek darpan sadaiv ek aabhas, seedha aur chhota pratibimb banata hai. Darpan ki pahchan kijiye aur isse pratibimb nirman darshan ke liye namankit kiran aarekhi banaiye.
questions.text_english: A mirror always forms a virtual, erect, and diminished image. Identify the mirror and draw a labelled ray diagram to show image formation.

key_points: The mirror is a convex mirror (uttal darpan).
Convex mirrors always form virtual, erect, and diminished images irrespective of object position.
Ray diagram: two rays from object - one parallel to principal axis (reflects as if coming from focus), one directed at centre of curvature (reflects back).

questions.image_description: A ray diagram showing a convex mirror with an object placed in front of it. Two rays are drawn from the top of the object: one parallel to the principal axis that reflects appearing to diverge from the focus, and one directed towards the centre of curvature that reflects back along the same path. The virtual, erect, and diminished image is formed behind the mirror.
questions.solution: The mirror is a convex mirror (also called a diverging mirror). It always forms a virtual, erect, and diminished image irrespective of the object's position. The ray diagram shows two incident rays from the object: one parallel to the principal axis reflecting as if coming from the focus (F), and another ray directed towards the centre of curvature (C) which reflects back along its own path. The reflected rays appear to diverge from a point behind the mirror, forming a virtual, erect, and smaller image.
questions.solution_hindi: Yah uttal darpan (convex mirror) hai jo sadaiv aabhas, sidha aur chhota pratibimb banata hai. Kiran aarekhi mein: ek kiran mukhli aksh ke samantar aati hai aur fokus se aati hui prakit hoti hai; dusri kiran vakra kendra ki aur jaati hai aur vaapis usi marg se paravartit hoti hai. Pratibimb darpan ke peechhe banta hai.

questions.text:
(ka) Bahya chumbkiya kshetra mein rakha koi dharavahi chalak ek bal ka anubhav karta hai, is tathy ko darshaane ke liye ek kriyakalap ka varnan kijiye.
(kha) Kalpna kijiye ki aap kisi chamber mein apni peeth ko kisi ek diwar se lagakar baithe hain. Koi electron-punj aapke peechhe ki diwar se samne vali diwar ki or kshitij gaman karte hue kisi prabal chumbkiya kshetra dwara aapke daayi or vikshepit ho jaata hai. Chumbkiya kshetra ki disha gyat kijiye.
questions.text_english:
(a) Describe an activity to show that a current-carrying conductor placed in an external magnetic field experiences a force.
(b) Imagine you are sitting in a chamber with your back against one wall. An electron beam moving horizontally from the back wall towards the front wall is deflected to your right by a strong magnetic field. Determine the direction of the magnetic field.

sub_questions.text: Dharavahi chalak par chumbkiya bal darshaane ke liye kriyakalap.
sub_questions.text_english: Activity to show force on current-carrying conductor in magnetic field.

key_points: Suspend an aluminium rod between poles of a horseshoe magnet. Pass current through the rod - it gets displaced.
Reverse current direction - rod moves in opposite direction.
This demonstrates the motor effect: force on current-carrying conductor in magnetic field.

sub_questions.solution: Take a horseshoe magnet and suspend an aluminium rod between its poles using connecting wires. When current is passed through the rod, it is displaced. Reversing the current direction reverses the displacement. This demonstrates Fleming's left-hand rule - a current-carrying conductor placed perpendicular to a magnetic field experiences a force perpendicular to both the current and field direction.

sub_questions.text: Chumbkiya kshetra ki disha gyat kijiye.
sub_questions.text_english: Determine direction of magnetic field.

key_points: Using Fleming's left-hand rule: electron (negative) beam moving forward is opposite to conventional current direction (backward).
Force is to the right, so magnetic field direction is upward (vertically).

sub_questions.solution: The electron beam moves from back to front. Since electrons are negatively charged, the conventional current direction is opposite - from front to back. The force is towards the right. Using Fleming's left-hand rule: point forefinger (field), middle finger (current), thumb (force) perpendicular. With current backward, force right, the magnetic field direction must be vertically downward (into the floor).

key_points: See sub_questions

questions.solution: (a) Activity: aluminium rod between magnet poles, pass current - rod moves. Reverse current - rod moves opposite. Shows force on current-carrying conductor in magnetic field. (b) Electron beam frontward, deflected right. Using left-hand rule (current backward, force right): magnetic field is vertically downward.
questions.solution_hindi: (ka) Kriyakalap: aluminium chhad ko magnet ke dhruvon ke beech talak tipaye, vidhyut pravaahit karein - chhad gatisheel hoti hai. Yah darshata hai ki dharavahi chalak chumbkiya kshetra mein bal anubhav karta hai. (kha) Electron beam aage, bal daen: chumbkiya kshetra ki disha neeche ki or (uttar se dakshin).

questions.text:
(ka) Ek dharavahi taar ke karan chumbkiya kshetra ka pattern us taar dwara banayee gayi aakriti par nirbhar karta hai. Pushthi kijiye.
(kha) Diye gaye chitra mein ek dharavahi sidha taar dikhayi gaya hai. P, Q aur R vidhyut mein se kis bindu par chumbkiya kshetra ki tivrata adhiktam hogi aur kyon?
questions.text_english:
(a) The magnetic field pattern due to a current-carrying wire depends on the shape formed by the wire. Justify.
(b) In the given figure, a current-carrying straight wire is shown. At which point P, Q, or R will the magnetic field intensity be maximum and why?

sub_questions.text: Dharavahi taar ke karan chumbkiya kshetra pattern ki pushthi.
sub_questions.text_english: Justify magnetic field pattern dependence on wire shape.

key_points: Straight wire: circular magnetic field lines around the wire.
Circular loop: magnetic field lines pass through centre, similar to a bar magnet.
Solenoid: uniform magnetic field inside, similar to a bar magnet.

sub_questions.solution: The magnetic field pattern depends on current-carrying wire shape. A straight wire produces concentric circular field lines around it. A circular loop produces field lines similar to a bar magnet, with maximum at the centre. A solenoid produces a uniform magnetic field inside, similar to a bar magnet, with field lines emerging from one end and entering the other.

sub_questions.text: Kis bindu par chumbkiya kshetra tivrata adhiktam hogi?
sub_questions.text_english: At which point is magnetic field intensity maximum?

key_points: Point P (closest to the wire) will have maximum magnetic field intensity.
Magnetic field strength is inversely proportional to distance from the wire (B proportional to 1/r).

sub_questions.solution: Point P will have the maximum magnetic field intensity as it is closest to the current-carrying wire. For a straight current-carrying conductor, the magnetic field strength (B) at a point is inversely proportional to its perpendicular distance from the wire (B proportional to 1/r). Therefore, the closer the point, the stronger the magnetic field.

key_points: See sub_questions

questions.image_description: A diagram showing a straight current-carrying wire with three points P, Q, and R at different distances from the wire. Point P is closest to the wire, followed by Q, then R which is farthest.
questions.solution: (a) Wire shape affects magnetic field: straight wire has concentric circles, loop has field like bar magnet, solenoid has uniform field inside. (b) Point P (closest to wire) has maximum field since B proportional to 1/r.
questions.solution_hindi: (ka) Taar ki aakriti ke anusar chumbkiya kshetra: sidhe taar ke liye sankendrit vritt, loop ke liye bar magnet jaise, solenoid ke liye saman kshetra. (kha) Bindu P par adhiktam kshetra kyonki duri nyuntam hai.

questions.text:
(ka) Tyndal prabhav kya hota hai?
(kha) Kya hota hai jab surya ka prakash bahut bade aakaar ke kanon se prakshirn hit hota hai?
(ga) Khatra darshane vale sanket sadaiv laal rang ke hote hain. Kyon?
questions.text_english:
(a) What is the Tyndall effect?
(b) What happens when sunlight is scattered by very large-sized particles?
(c) Danger signals are always red in colour. Why?

sub_questions.text: Tyndal prabhav kya hota hai?
sub_questions.text_english: What is the Tyndall effect?

key_points: Scattering of light by colloidal particles in their path, making the beam visible.

sub_questions.solution: The Tyndall effect is the phenomenon of scattering of light by colloidal particles (like dust, smoke, or water droplets) present in a medium. When a beam of light passes through a colloidal solution, the particles scatter the light, making the beam visible. For example, the visible beam of light in a dark room or the blue colour of the sky.

sub_questions.text: Surya ka prakash bade kanon se prakshirnit hone par kya hota hai?
sub_questions.text_english: What happens when sunlight is scattered by large particles?

key_points: Large particles scatter all colours of white light equally, making the scattered light appear white.

sub_questions.solution: When sunlight is scattered by very large-sized particles (like dust or water droplets in clouds), all colours of white light are scattered approximately equally. As a result, the scattered light appears white. This is why clouds appear white - they contain large water droplets that scatter all colours equally.

sub_questions.text: Khatra darshane vale sanket laal rang ke kyon?
sub_questions.text_english: Why are danger signals red?

key_points: Red light has the longest wavelength and is scattered the least by atmospheric particles.
Red light can travel longer distances through fog, smoke, and mist, making it visible from far away.

sub_questions.solution: Danger signals are red because red light has the longest wavelength among visible colours and is scattered the least by atmospheric particles like fog, smoke, or dust. Due to minimal scattering, red light can travel through the atmosphere over long distances without significant loss of intensity. This makes red signals visible from far away, ensuring timely warning even in adverse weather conditions.

key_points: See sub_questions

questions.solution: Tyndall effect: scattering of light by colloidal particles. Large particles scatter all colours equally -> white light. Red signals: red has longest wavelength, scattered least, visible farthest.
questions.solution_hindi: Tyndal prabhav: colloidal kanon dwara prakash ka prakshirn. Bade kan sabhi rangon ko saman roop se bikherte hain -> shvet prakat. Laal sanket: laal ki tarangdairghya sabse adhik, prakshirn sabse kam, door tak dikhai deta hai.

questions.text:
Lens apni fokal doori aur bimb ki sthiti ke aadhaar par vibhinn prakar ke pratibimb bana sakte hain. Ek uttal lens vastavik, ulta athva aabhas, sidha pratibimb banata hai jabki avtal lens keval aabhas aur chhota pratibimb banata hai. Fokal doori lens ki kshamta nirdharit karti hai. Paripati ke anusar uttal lens ki fokal doori dhanatmak hoti hai jabki avtal lens ki fokal doori rinatmak hoti hai. Jab lenson ko paraspar sampark mein rakha jaata hai, to unki kul kshamta lenson ki prithak-prithak kshamtaon ke yog se nirdharit hoti hai. Kiran aarekhi yah darshane mein sahayata karti hain ki prakash lens ke madhyam se kis prakar abhisarit ya apasarit hokar pratibimb banate hain.

(ka) Kisi 20 cm fokal doori vale uttal lens ka upayog pratibimb banane ke liye kiya gaya hai. Yadi koi bimb lens se 40 cm ki doori par rakha hai, to pratibimb ki sthiti aur prakriti kya hogi?
(kha) Kiran aarekhi ki sahayata se us sthiti mein pratibimb nirman darshaayiye jab bimb avtal lens ke mukhye fokus aur prakashik kendra ke beech rakha ho.
(ga) (i) Ek lens sanyojan mein, ek 30 cm fokal doori ka uttal lens aur -5 cm fokal doori ka avtal lens ek saath sampark mein rakhe hain. Is sanyojan ki tulya fokal doori aur kshamta gyat kijiye.
Athava
(ga) (ii) Do lens sampark mein rakhe hain. Ek -2 D fokal doori ka avtal lens hai aur doosra +3 D fokal doori ka uttal lens hai. Yah sanyojan kis prakar ke lens (uttal athva avtal) ke roop mein vyavahar karega? Karan dijiye.
questions.text_english:
Lenses can form different types of images depending on their focal length and object position. A convex lens forms a real, inverted or virtual, erect image, while a concave lens only forms a virtual and diminished image. Focal length determines lens power. By convention, focal length of convex lens is positive and of concave lens is negative. When lenses are placed in contact, total power is the sum of individual powers.

(a) A convex lens of focal length 20 cm is used to form an image. If the object is placed 40 cm from the lens, what is the position and nature of the image?
(b) Show image formation using a ray diagram when object is placed between the principal focus and optical centre of a concave lens.
(c) (i) In a lens combination, a convex lens of focal length 30 cm and a concave lens of focal length -5 cm are placed in contact. Find the equivalent focal length and power.
OR
(c) (ii) Two lenses are in contact: a concave lens of power -2 D and a convex lens of power +3 D. What type of lens (convex or concave) will this combination behave as? Give reason.

sub_questions.text: Pratibimb ki sthiti aur prakriti bataaiye.
sub_questions.text_english: Find image position and nature for convex lens with f=20 cm, u=-40 cm.

key_points: u = -40 cm, f = +20 cm. Using lens formula: 1/v - 1/u = 1/f gives v = +40 cm.
Image is real, inverted, and same size as object (formed at 2F).

sub_questions.solution: Given f = +20 cm, u = -40 cm. Using the lens formula 1/v - 1/u = 1/f: 1/v - 1/(-40) = 1/20. 1/v + 1/40 = 1/20. 1/v = 1/20 - 1/40 = 2/40 - 1/40 = 1/40. v = +40 cm. Since v is positive and u = v = 40 cm, the image is real, inverted, and same size as the object (object at 2F gives image at 2F).

sub_questions.text: Avtal lens mein bimb fokus aur kendra ke beech rakha hai - kiran aarekhi.
sub_questions.text_english: Ray diagram for concave lens - object between focus and optical centre.

key_points: Two rays: ray parallel to axis appears to diverge from focus on same side, ray through optical centre passes undeviated.
Image is virtual, erect, and diminished, formed on the same side as the object between focus and optical centre.

sub_questions.solution: When the object is placed between the principal focus (F) and the optical centre (O) of a concave lens, two rays are drawn. The first ray parallel to the principal axis appears to diverge from the focus on the same side. The second ray through the optical centre passes straight without deviation. These rays appear to meet on the same side as the object, producing a virtual, erect, and diminished image between F and O.

sub_questions.text: Lens sanyojan ki tulya fokal doori aur kshamta gyat kijiye.
sub_questions.text_english: Find equivalent focal length and power of lens combination.
sub_questions.solution: Power of convex lens: P1 = 100/f(cm) = 100/30 = +3.33 D. Power of concave lens: P2 = 100/(-5) = -20 D. Total power: P = P1 + P2 = 3.33 + (-20) = -16.67 D. Equivalent focal length: F = 100/P = 100/(-16.67) = -6 cm. Since total power is negative, the combination behaves as a concave (diverging) lens.

sub_questions.text: Sanyojan kis prakar ke lens ke roop mein vyavahar karega?
sub_questions.text_english: What type of lens does the combination behave as?

key_points: Since total power is positive, the combination behaves as a convex (converging) lens.

sub_questions.solution: Power of concave lens P1 = -2 D. Power of convex lens P2 = +3 D. Total power P = P1 + P2 = -2 + 3 = +1 D. Since the total power is positive (+1 D), the combination behaves as a convex (converging) lens with focal length f = 1/P = 1 m = 100 cm. The convex lens's power dominates over the concave lens's power.

sub_questions.text: Paripath ka kul pratirodh gyat kijiye.
sub_questions.text_english: Find total resistance of the circuit.

key_points: Two 20 and 10 ohm in parallel: 1/Rp = 1/20 + 1/10 = 3/20, Rp = 20/3 = 6.67 ohm

sub_questions.solution: The circuit shows a 20 ohm and 10 ohm resistor connected in parallel. The equivalent parallel resistance is calculated as: 1/Rp = 1/20 + 1/10 = 1/20 + 2/20 = 3/20. Therefore, Rp = 20/3 = 6.67 ohm.

sub_questions.text: Srot se li gayi kul vaidhyut dhara gyat kijiye.
sub_questions.text_english: Find total current drawn from source.
sub_questions.solution: Using Ohm's law, total current I = V/Req = 10 / (20/3) = 10 * 3/20 = 1.5 A. The source provides 1.5 amperes of current to the parallel combination of resistors.

sub_questions.text: 3 ohm pratirodhak ke sir per vibhavantar gyat kijiye. (Note: OCR unclear, adapting based on context)
sub_questions.text_english: Find potential difference across 3 ohm resistor. (Adapting - may be different resistor in actual paper)

key_points: In parallel circuit, voltage across each branch = source voltage = 10 V.

sub_questions.solution: Assuming the 3 ohm resistor is in one branch of a parallel combination. In parallel circuits, the voltage across all branches is equal to the source voltage. Hence the potential difference across the 3 ohm resistor would be 10 V. Current through it would be I = V/R = 10/3 = 3.33 A.

sub_questions.text: Pashv kram mein bulbs ke liye maing se li gayi dhara gyat kijiye.
sub_questions.text_english: Calculate mains current for bulbs in parallel.
sub_questions.solution: For bulb 1 (100 W, 220 V): I1 = P1/V = 100/220 = 0.455 A. For bulb 2 (60 W, 220 V): I2 = P2/V = 60/220 = 0.273 A. In parallel connection, total current is the sum of individual currents: I = I1 + I2 = 0.455 + 0.273 = 0.728 A.

sub_questions.text: Ohm ke niyam ka kathan likhiye aur V-I graph banaaiye.
sub_questions.text_english: State Ohm's law and draw V-I graph.

key_points: Ohm's law: At constant temperature, current flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across its ends.
V = IR, graph is a straight line through origin. Slope = V/I = R.

sub_questions.solution: Ohm's law states that at constant physical conditions (temperature), the current flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference applied across its ends: V proportional to I, or V = IR, where R is the constant of proportionality called resistance. The V-I graph is a straight line passing through the origin. The slope of this graph (V/I) gives the resistance of the conductor.

sub_questions.text: Shreni kram mein kul pratirodh ke liye vyanyak vyutpann kijiye.
sub_questions.text_english: Derive expression for total resistance in series combination.

key_points: In series, same current flows through all resistors.
V = V1 + V2 + V3 = IR1 + IR2 + IR3 = I(R1 + R2 + R3)
Req = V/I = R1 + R2 + R3

sub_questions.solution: In series combination, the same current I flows through all resistors R1, R2, and R3. The total potential difference V across the combination equals the sum of individual potential differences: V = V1 + V2 + V3. Using Ohm's law: V1 = IR1, V2 = IR2, V3 = IR3. Therefore, V = I(R1 + R2 + R3). If Req is the equivalent resistance, then V = I(Req). Hence, Req = R1 + R2 + R3. The total resistance in series is the sum of individual resistances.
